## Quick start

The root package requires Go 1.24 or newer and has no external runtime dependencies. The complete example catalog includes optional SDK drivers and uses Go 1.26 or newer. This library is unreleased. Clone and run the canonical example:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/goforj/feature.git
cd feature
go -C examples run ./quickstart
```

The example constructs an injected client, then enables checkout for a selected tenant:

```go
{{QUICKSTART}}
```

## Available sources

Both sources are included in the root module:

| Source | Scope | Updates |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MemorySource | One process, no persistence | Replace the document, then refresh clients. |
| FileSource | A regular local JSON file or symlink | Read the path on refresh, including atomic file replacement. |

Source configuration is explicit. The library does not read or modify `.env`, start a global client, or require a flag-management service. See the [versioned JSON contract](docs/contract.md) for targeting rules, limits, failure behavior, and multi-process consistency.

## SDK drivers

The optional adapters keep vendor dependencies and Go requirements outside the root module:

| Driver | Constructors | Minimum Go | Verification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [LaunchDarkly](driver/launchdarklyfeature) | New borrows an SDK client; Open owns initialization and shutdown. | 1.25 | Real SDK, local streaming and analytics, startup failures, and shutdown. |
| [OpenFeature](driver/openfeaturefeature) | New borrows a client; Open owns an isolated API and provider. | 1.26 | Real GO Feature Flag Docker service in remote and in-process modes, plus the LaunchDarkly provider. |

Every runtime module requires exact 100% unit statement coverage. The separate [integration suite](integration) checks real services and SDK transports with race detection; its [execution report](docs/integration-results.json) identifies tested versions and source. Hosted LaunchDarkly account verification remains pending. Features is the portable application API; native Client retains source refresh and genuine snapshots.

## Runnable examples

Run from the repository root:

```sh
go -C examples run ./quickstart   # Identity targeting and explicit fallback.
go -C examples run ./portable     # Portable checks and typed request targeting.
go -C examples run ./targeting    # Attributes and stable percentage rollout.
go -C examples run ./refresh      # File replacement and request snapshots.
go -C examples run ./polling      # Owned, cancellable refresh loop.
go -C examples run ./launchdarkly # Borrowed and owned SDK adapters, offline data.
go -C examples run ./openfeature  # Borrowed and owned SDKs, memory provider.
```

Tests execute these programs and verify their output. Their source is authoritative: [quickstart](examples/quickstart/main.go), [targeting](examples/targeting/main.go), [refresh](examples/refresh/main.go), [polling](examples/polling/main.go), [LaunchDarkly](examples/launchdarkly/main.go), [OpenFeature](examples/openfeature/main.go).

The [portable example](examples/portable/main.go) shows the application-facing Features API. Native Client retains explicit source refresh and snapshot operations; Features borrows any Evaluator and provides short checks and owned targeting scopes.

## How it works

- **Local decisions:** evaluations perform no I/O. Rules match in order; otherwise the configured default applies.
- **Explicit fallback:** missing flags, invalid inputs, or canceled evaluations use the caller's fallback. Evaluate explains the result.
- **Complete publication:** refresh validates a full document before publishing one immutable revision.
- **Failure retention:** refresh failures retain the previous revision. Initial load failures prevent construction.
- **Process boundaries:** each process refreshes independently. Shared documents provide eventual convergence, with no fleet-wide atomic switch.

## Development

```sh
make test-unit       # Execute tests and examples; require exact library coverage.
make test-race       # Include race instrumentation in executable examples.
make test-integration # Require Docker; test real services and SDK transports.
make vet
make record-unit     # Refresh tracked evidence after relevant source changes.
make generate
make check-generated
```

See [development](docs/development.md) for module ownership, validation commands, and publication status. Framework integration, hosted providers, and administration interfaces are separate from this standalone library.

The [remaining-work checklist](docs/roadmap.md) tracks library review, real-App validation, GoForj integration, and release preparation. The [provider study](docs/provider-study.md) records the design research; both initial SDK adapters and their local service integration suites are implemented.
